extracted.intended_audience: editors, journalists and newsrooms in the UK
extracted.subtask_description: Working definition and checklist used by UK editors under the IPSO Editors' Code to determine when intrusive or sensitive reporting can be justified by the public interest. Covers specific types of public-interest disclosure, the burden on editors when invoking the exception, implicit newsworthiness signals, and special considerations (children, subterfuge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting or exposing crime, or the threat of crime, or serious impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting or exposing crime, or the threat of crime, or serious impropriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary example of what counts as public interest; used to justify intrusive or sensitive reporting. Appears again in the page's implicit newsworthiness list as 'Crime exposure — fundamental.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting public health or safety
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts as public interest justification for reporting that may otherwise be intrusive or sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting the public from being misled
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting the public from being misled by an action or statement of an individual or organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames accountability reporting where the public may be misinformed as a public-interest justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing failures to comply with obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosing failures to comply with obligations (regulatory, legal, professional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes exposing regulatory, legal or professional non-compliance as a public-interest rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing a miscarriage of justice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miscarriages of justice are explicitly listed as public-interest grounds, supporting reporting that may reveal case details or mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising or contributing to a matter of public debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising or contributing to a matter of public debate, including serious cases of impropriety, unethical conduct or incompetence concerning the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers democratic and civic-value reporting where public discussion is materially advanced by publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing concealment, or likely concealment, of the above
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosing concealment, or likely concealment, of any of the above (crime, public-safety threats, misleading statements, failures to comply, miscarriages of justice, matters of public debate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposing attempts to hide wrongdoing or risks is itself a public-interest justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest in freedom of expression itself
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a public interest in freedom of expression itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognises that publication can be justified by the intrinsic public interest in free expression, separate from specific disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on editors: reasonable belief publication would serve the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking the public interest exception, editors must demonstrate that they reasonably believed publication would serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the evidential burden editors must meet when relying on the public interest; must be able to show this belief was held at the time of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on editors: proportionality of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking the public interest exception, editors must demonstrate they believed publication would be proportionate to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should balance intrusion against the public benefit and be able to justify why publication was proportionate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on editors: ability to explain decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking the public interest exception, editors must be able to explain how they reached that decision at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires contemporaneous reasoning/rationale so the decision to publish can be justified to regulators or complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit newsworthiness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit list of newsworthiness signals reinforcing public-interest considerations: crime exposure; public safety/health threat; misleading the public; hidden wrongdoing; justice failures; civic debate enrichment; concealment exposure; free expression value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These implicit criteria reiterate and underscore the kinds of stories likely to meet the public interest threshold; they function as heuristics for editorial judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration — children
rubrics_metrics.description: Children: editors must demonstrate exceptional public interest to override normally paramount interests of the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The welfare and privacy of children are given special weight; only exceptional public-interest cases may justify intrusive reporting involving children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration — subterfuge and undercover reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Subterfuge / undercover reporting requires demonstrable public interest justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of deception or covert methods must be justified by a clear and demonstrable public interest reason before being relied upon.
